   177	\section{What the cited soundness theorem requires: the import obligations}
   178	\label{sec:import-obligations}
   179	
   180	The quantum soundness theorem for the classical game inherits the constraint
   181	$m' \mid q$ solely because it is stated for the game just described; its
   182	proof fixes an admissible $q$ with $m' \mid q$, asserts that the game with
   183	simultaneity parameter $1$ is \emph{identical} to the two-prover tensor-code
   184	test for the Reed--Solomon tensor code $\mathcal C^{\ot m'}$ of the same
   185	authors' \emph{Quantum soundness of testing tensor codes} (arXiv:2111.08131)
   186	\cite{Ji2021Quantum}, and concludes by Theorem~4.7 there, instantiated with
   187	that theorem's auxiliary integer parameter --- denoted $k$ in that source,
   188	and written $K$ here to avoid clashing with the field exponent and the
   189	simultaneity parameter --- chosen as $(m')^3 d$.  Neither
   190	the asserted identity nor the instantiation is complete as stated, so the
   191	import carries two verification obligations, which this section details and
   192	which the blueprint's proof node for the soundness statement records as
   193	open for the printed tensor-code route. Both obligations are independent of
   194	the divisibility question and remain open for that route at every dimension
   195	where that game is defined.  They would also arise from an attempt to prove
   196	soundness of the directly indexed game by the same tensor-code import.  The
   197	established proof for the directly indexed game takes a different route through
   198	the low individual degree theorem and therefore bypasses both obligations.
   199	
   200	\paragraph{The cited test.}
   201	In the two-prover tensor-code test (Figures~1 and~2 of
   202	\cite{Ji2021Quantum}; the two-prover strategy format and the goodness
   203	measure are Definitions~4.5 and~4.6 there), the referee performs one of
   204	three subtests with probability $1/3$ each, assigning the two roles of each
   205	subtest to the two provers uniformly at random.  \emph{Axis-parallel lines
   206	test}: sample a uniform point $u \in [n]^{m'}$ and a uniform axis
   207	$j \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$; send the axis-parallel line $\ell$ through $u$ in
   208	direction $j$ to one prover, who answers a codeword $g \in \mathcal C$;
   209	send $u$ to the other, who answers a field value $a$; accept iff
   210	$g(u_j) = a$.  \emph{Subcube commutation test}: sample
   211	$j \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$ and a subcube $H \subseteq [n]^{m'}$ by fixing the
   212	last $j-1$ coordinates uniformly; sample $u, v$ independently and uniformly
   213	in $H$ and a uniform order bit; send the ordered pair $(u,v)$ or $(v,u)$ to
   214	one prover, who answers a pair $(b_u, b_v)$ of field values; send $u$ to
   215	the other, who answers $a$; accept iff $b_u = a$.  \emph{Synchronicity
   216	test}: send one identical question --- a line, a point, or an ordered
   217	pair, with probability $1/3$ each --- to both provers and accept iff their
   218	answers agree.  Theorem~4.7 supposes a two-prover strategy passing this
   219	test with probability $1-\eps$ together with an integer parameter
   220	$K \ge 12 m' t$, where $t$ is the interpolation parameter of the base code
   221	--- for the degree-$d$ Reed--Solomon code, of blocklength $n = q$ and
   222	distance $q-d$, one has $t = d+1$ --- and produces projective measurements
   223	$\{G_c\}$ and $\{\tilde G_c\}$ with outcomes in $\mathcal C^{\ot m'}$,
   224	consistent with one prover's points measurements, with the other prover's
   225	lines measurements, and with each other, up to
   226	$\eta'(m',t,K,\eps,n^{-1}) = \mathrm{poly}(m',t,K) \cdot
   227	\mathrm{poly}(\eps, n^{-1}, e^{-K/(m')^2})$.
   228	
   229	\paragraph{Obligation 1: the game correspondence.}
   230	The source asserts that the $\chi$-based game at parameters $(q,m',d,1)$
   231	is this test.  It is not, in four respects.
   232	(i)~The game has no pair questions.  A pair question of the test reveals
   233	two points of a \emph{hidden} subcube --- the subcube itself is not sent
   234	--- and is answered by two field values, while the game's diagonal-line
   235	question reveals a full line description and is answered by a degree-$m'd$
   236	polynomial.  A reduction must construct the pair measurements from the
   237	diagonal-line measurements by post-processing (measure a line through $u$
   238	and $v$ and evaluate the answered polynomial at the two parameters), and
   239	both directions of the information mismatch matter: the game's line
   240	description carries an index and a seed, neither of which is a function of
   241	the pair $(u,v)$, so the constructed measurement must average over the
   242	compatible indices and seeds; and the game's diagonal lines fix the
   243	\emph{first} $i-1$ coordinates where the test's subcubes fix the
   244	\emph{last} $j-1$, so the coordinate conventions must be aligned.  The
   245	construction must preserve projectivity and must match the law of the
   246	hidden-subcube pair with the law induced by the game's diagonal sampling.
   247	(ii)~The game's line questions carry the seed $s \in \F_q$; the test's carry
   248	only the line.  A strategy may depend on the seed beyond its class
   249	$\chi^{-1}(i)$.  For the comparison with the directly indexed game, this
   250	dependence is now retained in a correlated residue register rather than
   251	averaged away, as explained below.  That construction resolves this part of
   252	the direct-game transport, but it has not been composed with the distinct
   253	pair-question construction required for the tensor-code test.
   254	(iii)~The branch weights differ: each nontrivial cross-test has mass $1/3$
   255	in the test against $2/9$ in the game.  Once the per-branch predicates are
   256	matched, the intended bookkeeping bound is that the constructed strategy's
   257	rejection probability in the test is at most $\tfrac32$ times the game's
   258	rejection probability, up to the $O(1/(m'q))$ of item~(iv); this bound is
   259	the target of the obligation, not an established fact.
   260	(iv)~The game's predicate fixes an acceptance convention on diagonal
   261	questions with zero direction --- an event of probability at most
   262	$2/(m'q)$, recorded in the blueprint's remark on zero directions --- for
   263	which the test has no counterpart branch.
   264	Finally, the displayed conclusions of Theorem~4.7 pair one prover's points
   265	measurements with the other prover's tensor-codeword measurement, and the
   266	first prover's tensor-codeword measurement with the second prover's lines
   267	measurements, while the game-level statement asserts the point consistency
   268	in both directions; deriving the stated form uses the role symmetrization
   269	of the test and belongs to the correspondence.  None of these steps is
   270	difficult to state, but none is carried out in the source, and together
   271	they replace the asserted one-line identity by a reduction carrying its
   272	own value bound.
   273	
   274	\paragraph{Obligation 2: the parameter bound.}
   275	Theorem~4.7 requires $K \ge 12 m' t = 12 m' (d+1)$.  The source
   276	instantiates $K = (m')^3 d$, which meets the bound iff
   277	$(m')^2 d \ge 12(d+1)$: this holds for all $d \ge 1$ when $m' \ge 5$,
   278	holds at $m' = 4$ exactly when $d \ge 3$, and fails for every $d$ when
   279	$m' \le 3$.  In the game's parameter domain the dimension divides the
   280	admissible field size and is therefore a power of two, so the source's
   281	instantiation violates the hypothesis exactly at $m' \in \{1,2\}$ for
   282	every $d$ and at $m' = 4$ for $d \in \{1,2\}$ --- in particular, in the
   283	multilinear regime $d = 1$, at every dimension $m' \le 4$.  A candidate
   284	repair is to instantiate $K = \max((m')^3 d,\, 12 m'(d+1))$; the open
   285	obligation is then to re-absorb the error, that is, to check that
   286	$\mathrm{poly}(m',t,K)$ and $e^{-K/(m')^2}$ still collapse to the form
   287	$a(dm')^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bm'd})$ in the small-$m'$ cases where the
   288	maximum is $12m'(d+1)$ --- plausible, since there
   289	$e^{-K/(m')^2} = e^{-12(d+1)/m'}$ decays in $d$ at a rate comparable to
   290	$2^{-m'd}$ for $m' \le 4$, but not checked here.
   291	
   292	In the correspondence of Obligation~1, the only role of the divisibility
   293	$m' \mid q$ is to make the $\chi$-sampled index uniform.  The underlying
   294	mathematics does not need the divisibility.  The low
   295	individual degree test of \cite{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree} samples its axis
   296	index $i$ uniformly from $\{1,\ldots,m'\}$ directly, with no index function
   297	on $\F_q$ and no divisibility hypothesis,%
   298	\footnote{See the test figure in \path{references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex}.}
   299	and the tensor-code test is likewise a test about the code
   300	$\mathcal C^{\ot m'}$, not about an encoding of indices into $\F_q$.  The
   301	$\chi$-based packaging exists so that the question distribution is
   302	conditionally linear, which the introspection machinery requires for the
   303	game the players actually play --- the Pauli basis test at dimension $m$,
   304	where admissibility does supply the divisibility.  The game at dimension
   305	$2m+2$ never appears in a verifier; it is an internal analysis device in the
   306	proof of the polynomial-pair lemma, so nothing there requires its question
   307	distribution to be conditionally linear.

    70	Throughout, $(q,m,d)$ is an admissible parameter tuple of the Pauli basis

   123	\section{The domain of the conditional Lean helper}
   124	
   125	The source statement does not take an arbitrary joint point measurement as an
   126	input.  It uses the family $\{\hat Q^{x,z}_{a,b}\}$ constructed by the preceding
   127	point lemma, whose error has the form $\delta_Q(\eps)=\poly(\eps)$.  Consequently,
   128	an internal theorem which accepts an already constructed point witness must retain
   129	the same quantitative dependency: it should first fix a function
   130	$\delta_Q:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfying the one-variable polynomial-error
   131	predicate, then choose $\delta_P$, and at strategy error $\eps$ accept only a
   132	point witness with bound $\delta_Q(\eps)$.
   133	
   134	Before the repair tracked by \ghissue{389}, the Lean helper
   135	\path{exists_combinedLinesWitness_ofPointsWitness} instead had the quantifier
   136	order
   137	\[
   138	  \exists\delta_P=\poly(\eps,md/q)\quad
   139	  \forall\eps\ \forall\delta_Q\ \forall Q,
   140	  \qquad Q\text{ has point error at most }\delta_Q
   141	  \Longrightarrow T\text{ has line error at most }\delta_P(\eps,md/q).
   142	\]
   143	Thus the line-error function was chosen before an unrestricted scalar
   144	$\delta_Q$, and did not depend on it.  The fields of
   145	\path{CombinedPointsWitness} bound self-consistency and the two ordered-product
   146	comparisons by precisely this scalar; they impose no relation between an
   147	arbitrary $\delta_Q$ and $\eps$.  The conditioned-pasting estimate therefore
   148	cannot eliminate $\delta_Q$ from its conclusion.
   149	
   150	There is a concrete mathematical obstruction to the old domain.  Set
   151	$\eps=0$, take $m=1$ and fixed $d$, and let $q$ grow through admissible field
   152	sizes with $q>d+1$.  On any perfect strategy, define the supplied projective
   153	joint point measurement deterministically, with X answer $x^{d+1}$ and a fixed
   154	Z answer, identically on the two player sides.  Its self-consistency defect is
   155	zero, while the two ordered-product defects are finite and hence can be covered
   156	by a sufficiently large scalar $\delta_Q$, which the old helper quantified
   157	arbitrarily.  On an axis X line, however, every outcome allowed by

   218	\subsection{The extended-line supplied-point obstruction}
   219	
   220	The same quantitative omission appeared in the auxiliary
   221	\path{exists_extendedLinesWitness_ofPointsWitness}: a single polynomial error
   222	function is chosen before an arbitrary scalar $\delta_Q$ and every point witness
   223	at that error. Passing from paired points to the extended scalar answer does
   224	not remove this obstruction. The first-route estimate
   225	$C m g(\eps,md/q)$ in
   226	\path{exists_extendedLinesWitness_established_ofPointsWitness} had the same
   227	problem: it still tends to zero at $\eps=0$ with fixed $m,d$ and increasing $q$.
   228	These unrestricted auxiliaries were tracked by \ghissue{509} and \ghissue{511},
   229	respectively; neither signature survives, and the argument of this subsection is
   230	the reason why. Section~\ref{sec:supplied-point-realignment} records what
   231	replaced them. The source instead uses the family constructed by its point lemma,
   232	with $\delta_Q=\poly(\eps)$, and defines the scalar answer by
   233	$c=\alpha a+\beta b$. Claim~17-1 explicitly retains the point error.
   234	\footnote{The source passages are \path{lem:qld-4-10}, \path{lem:qld-4-12}, and
   235	\path{claim:17-1} in
   236	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex},
   237	lines~689--709, 993--1018, and 1140--1173.}
   238	
   239	Take $m=d=1$, $\eps=0$, and let $q=2^{2k+1}>2$ tend to infinity.
   240	These parameters are admissible. The Pauli basis test has a perfect projective strategy by
   241	\path{lem:pauli-completeness}.\footnote{See
   242	\path{references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex},
   243	lines~1229--1421, for the construction; the statement and its projective Pauli
   244	measurements appear at lines~1232--1255.}
   245	Let $\hat\psi$ be its normalized expanded state. On each player's expanded
   246	local space, define the supplied joint point measurement by
   247	\[
   248	 Q^{x,z}_{a,b}=
   249	 \begin{cases}
   250	   \Id,&(a,b)=(x^2,0),\\
   251	   0,&\text{otherwise}.
   252	 \end{cases}
   253	\]
   254	This is a complete projective measurement and is exactly self-consistent in
   255	every opposite placement. The finitely many averaged squared distances from the
   256	two ordered expanded point products are finite real numbers. Taking their
   257	maximum and zero gives a scalar $\delta_Q$ satisfying all the fields of the
   258	point witness. No estimate of this scalar in terms of $\eps$ is required.
   259	
   260	The extended point answer is $\alpha x^2$. In dimension $2m+2=4$, the directly
   261	indexed line-point law assigns weight $1/2$ to axis lines and then chooses one
   262	of the four coordinates uniformly. Its X-axis branch therefore has mass $1/8$.
   263	On that branch, $z,\alpha,\beta$ are fixed along the line, while $x$ is uniform
   264	in the field. The canonical base has X coordinate zero, so the affine line
   265	parameter is exactly $x$. For $\alpha\ne0$, every permitted line answer $p$
   266	has degree at most one, and $p(X)-\alpha X^2$ is a nonzero polynomial of degree
   267	two. It has at most two roots, hence its agreement with the point answer is at
   268	most $2/q$.
   269	
   270	This bound also holds for any line POVM. Indeed, for a fixed line let $w_p$
   271	be the expectation of its effect for $p$ in the expanded state, at the line
   272	player's placement. Positivity and completeness give $w_p\ge0$ and
   273	$\sum_p w_p=1$; the axis-degree field makes $w_p=0$ for higher-degree answers.
   274	The opposite point effect is deterministically the identity at $\alpha x^2$,
   275	so the agreement is precisely the $w_p$-weighted average of those root-count
   276	fractions. These weights depend on the line but not on $x$ along it. Averaging
   277	over the fixed coordinates, and using nonnegativity of the defect on the
   278	remaining question branches, gives for either player orientation
   279	\[
   280	 \operatorname{defect}\ \ge\
   281	 \frac18\left(1-\frac1q\right)\left(1-\frac2q\right).
   282	\]
   283	There is no undefined evaluation on these nonzero axis directions, so the
   284	completed answer alphabet does not change this calculation. The scalar field
   285	identification preserves the polynomial evaluations and their root counts.
   286	
   287	The lower bound tends to $1/8$. In contrast, the predicate
   288	\path{IsPolyErr}\textsubscript{2} bounds the proposed error at these parameters by
   289	$\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}(0,1/q)\le Cq^{-s}$ with $s>0$, which tends to zero.
   290	For the first-route estimate, the polynomial-error bound on $g$ likewise gives
   291	fixed constants $K\ge1$ and $r,s>0$ with
   292	$C g(0,1/q)\le CKq^{-s}\longrightarrow0$.
   293	Consequently both unrestricted supplied-point auxiliaries are false,
   294	independently of the printed-error discrepancy and the diagonal-line degeneracy.
   295	This argument does not refute the existential point-witness declarations or the source
   296	\path{lem:qld-4-13}; neither requires a line approximation to every arbitrarily
   297	chosen point family.

    40	\section{Key theorem forms}
    41	
    42	Let $H_X$ and $H_Z$ be the positive contractions of the extraction proof, and
    43	let $\vartheta$ be a unit vector such that
    44	\[
    45	  \langle\vartheta,H_W\vartheta\rangle\geq1-\delta/2
    46	  \qquad (W\in\{X,Z\}).
    47	\]
    48	Since $(I-H_W)^2\geq0$,
    49	\[
    50	  H_W^2\geq2H_W-I,
    51	  \qquad
    52	  \langle\vartheta,H_W^2\vartheta\rangle\geq1-\delta.
    53	\]
    54	Also $\lVert(I-H_W)\vartheta\rVert^2\leq\delta$, whence
    55	\[
    56	  \lVert H_X\vartheta-H_Z\vartheta\rVert^2\leq4\delta.
    57	\]
    58	Together with $H_XH_Z$ equal to the EPR projection, these estimates give the
    59	required overlap bound, with constants absorbed into the stated
    60	$O(\sqrt\delta)$ error.
    61	
    62	For the final transfer, let $\phi\colon\mathcal H\to\mathcal K$ be an isometry
    63	and set $Q=\phi\phi^\dagger$.  If $N_h$ is the unitary-conjugated extension of
    64	a measurement operator $M_h$, then the exact identity is
    65	\[
    66	  \phi M_h\phi^\dagger=N_hQ=QN_h,
    67	\]
    68	not merely $N_h$.  Thus comparison of $N_h$ with an ideal projector must be
    69	combined with control of $(I-Q)\Delta$ on the ideal comparison state
    70	$\Delta$.

    95	\section{The range-projection obligation}
    96	
    97	Lines~1827--1858 prove state-dependent closeness for the concrete operators
    98	obtained by conjugating the original measurement with the swap unitaries.
    99	Lines~1864--1875 then define isometries by adjoining EPR pairs and applying
   100	those unitaries, and immediately state the corresponding closeness for
   101	$\phi M_h\phi^\dagger$.  The omitted range projection makes this implication
   102	non-definitional \cite[lines~1827--1875]{Ji2020MIPStar}.
   103	
   104	Let $\Psi$ be the original state and suppose $\phi\Psi$ is close to the ideal
   105	state $\Delta$.  Since $Q\phi\Psi=\phi\Psi$ and $Q$ is a contraction, the
   106	triangle inequality bounds $(I-Q)\Delta$ by the state-extraction error.  Using
   107	$\phi M_h\phi^\dagger=N_hQ$, split
   108	\[
   109	  (N_hQ-T_h)\Delta
   110	  =(N_h-T_h)\Delta-N_h(I-Q)\Delta,
   111	\]
   112	where $T_h$ is the ideal Pauli projector.  Summing squared norms over $h$
   113	uses projectivity and orthogonality to keep the second term under control.
   114	The same argument is required for each player and each Pauli basis.
   115	
   116	The finite-dimensional estimate is proved in
   117	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/Soundness/RangeProjection.lean}. For a complete POVM
   118	$\{N_h\}$, an orthogonal projection $Q$, and $Q\vartheta=\vartheta$, it gives
   119	\[
   120	  \sum_h\|(N_hQ-T_h)\Delta\|^2
   121	  \le 2\sum_h\|(N_h-T_h)\Delta\|^2+2\|\Delta-\vartheta\|^2.
   122	\]
   123	The proof uses $\sum_h N_h^\dagger N_h\le I$, so it also applies when the
   124	measurement is not projective. The same module proves the isometry form under
   125	the exact identity $N_h\phi=\phi M_h$ and its two bipartite placements. The
   126	unit-ancilla embedding and its composition with a unitary, including the
   127	identity $U(M\ot I\ot I)U^\dagger\phi=\phi M$, are proved in
   128	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/Soundness/Ancilla.lean} for $\phi=UJ$,
   129	$J\psi=\psi\ot\eta$, $\|\eta\|=1$, and $U^\dagger U=I$.
   130	
   131	The supplied-data transfer is proved in
   132	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/Soundness/StateTransfer.lean} and
   133	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/Soundness/OperatorTransfer.lean}. Given an actual
   134	\path{ExtractionWitness}, the local maps adjoin a normalized EPR state and
   135	apply its swap unitaries. Register reassociation identifies their tensor
   136	action with the witness's transformed state, so its squared distance from
   137	the ideal state is at most $\delta$. The existing swapped total-Pauli POVMs
   138	intertwine with these maps; the two bipartite range-projection estimates
   139	bound each full squared operator-family sum by $4\delta$. Thus the same
   140	\path{PauliSoundnessWitness} satisfies all three soundness estimates at
   141	$\max\{\sqrt\delta,4\delta\}$. This is an auxiliary result with supplied
   142	extraction data, not a new bridge field or a proof of soundness for arbitrary
   143	strategies.

   262	\section{Conclusion}
   263	
   264	The printed triangle calculation has repairable numerical errors, and the
   265	last passage from unitaries to isometries omits a genuine range-projection
   266	argument.  Neither defect is a counterexample to Pauli soundness.  The former
   267	is corrected by positive-contraction inequalities and a small-error split;
   268	the latter has a proved general estimate and an application to the concrete
   269	extraction data. The global polynomial-pair witness
   270	and the three pulled-apart consistency estimates are now composed in a proved
   271	source-facing theorem, including at zero error. The conditional extraction
   272	theorem remains useful for a supplied global measurement, and its composition
   273	with the proved global constructor establishes the source-facing existence
   274	claim of Lemma~\path{lem:qld-unitary} for projective strategies. Its concrete
   275	isometry transfer, including the state and both operator estimates, is proved
   276	for supplied extraction data. Composing that transfer with the internally
   277	constructed data proves the restricted projective-setting isometry bounds.
   278	The Naimark reduction then removes the projectivity restriction with exact
   279	value preservation, the operator-family transfer returns both Pauli families
   280	to the original spaces at $3\delta + 6\delta^2$, the scalar absorption returns
   281	that shape to the robustness form at prefactor $21a^2$, and monotonicity in
   282	the error parameter carries the bounds to the rest of the source error
   283	domain.  Composing these with the projective-setting bounds proves

1	# Completion protocol — definition of done
     2	
     3	Normative. This protocol says when a formalization **track** may be declared
     4	finished, and forbids the declaration until a model-free gate agrees. Amend it
     5	only through `local/protocols/meta.md` (`EVOLUTION.md` entry, cited trigger).
     6	
     7	Trigger for its existence, owner, 2026-09-19: *"some protocol(s) in the
     8	workflow should ensure that when the project finishes, the formalization is
     9	done without caveat, and satisfies the lean comparator"*; earlier the same day,
    10	*"i want zero sorry"*.
    11	
    12	## 1. Scope
    13	
    14	A **track** is a Lean subtree, the blueprint chapters describing it, its
    15	paper-gap register, its axiom-audit file, its blueprint exemption table, its
    16	comparator record and its artifact file set. The per-track data is §6; QPBT is
    17	the only track registered
    18	today, but nothing here is QPBT-specific.
    19	
    20	**Declaring finished** means any public statement that the track is complete: a
    21	completion comment on its umbrella issues (27/168 for QPBT), closing those
    22	issues, tagging a release, or a README/status page that says the track is done.
    23	
    24	## 2. Finished without caveat
    25	
    26	A track is finished without caveat at a commit when all seven criteria hold *at
    27	that commit*.
    28	
    29	**C1 — Proof integrity.** Zero term-level `sorry`, `admit`, project `axiom` or
    30	`constant` declaration, `native_decide` / `decide +native`, or
    31	`Lean.trustCompiler` under the track's Lean root. The sorry-site rule is the
    32	one in `results/telemetry/owner-tools/estimate.sh` (`SORRY_SITE_RE`), and there
    33	is exactly **one** implementation of it: `scripts/completion_gate.py` loads that
    34	line from that file and never restates it. Explicit axiom declarations are
    35	found with `DECL_RE` of `scripts/audit_lean_axiom_declarations.py`, imported
    36	rather than copied.
    37	
    38	**C2 — Headline axioms.** Every headline theorem of §6 depends only on
    39	`propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. The check is a committed
    40	`AxiomAudit` Lean file for the track that carries one audit command per
    41	headline theorem — `assert_standard_axioms` (LDT) or `audit_standard_axioms`
    42	(the command QPBT's audit module defines); both print the axiom set and fail
    43	elaboration unless it is exactly those three — and is built in CI. The gate
    44	checks that the file
    45	exists and covers the table; the axiom values themselves come from the build
    46	and are reported as delegated.
    47	
    48	**C3 — Paper gaps terminal.** Every data row of the track's paper-gap register
    49	carries a `Terminal status` cell reading exactly `corrected` or
    50	`no-difference`:
    51	
    52	- `corrected` — a documented statement correction that **meets the four
    53	  adoption conditions of `local/protocols/issues-prs.md`** — correctness,
    54	  sufficiency, minimality ("the closest sufficient statement to the source,
    55	  with no unnecessary hypothesis or weakened conclusion and no change to the
    56	  source semantics") and Lean convergence — and carries its three artifacts: a
    57	  gap note, a corrected blueprint node citing it, and, where the printed claim
    58	  is not proved, the printed claim preserved as a non-asserted `Prop` (the
    59	  `lem:symmetric-strat` and `lem:qld-4-13` pattern of 2026-09-19). The
    60	  artifacts are evidence that a correction was adopted; they are not a route
    61	  around those conditions, and a row whose correction weakens a conclusion is
    62	  not terminal however complete its artifacts are.
    63	- `no-difference` — the formalization and the source statement agree; nothing
    64	  to correct.
    65	
    66	No row may read `open`, `pending` or `sorry`. No headline theorem statement may
    67	be weaker than the source paper except through a `corrected` row.
    68	
    69	**C4 — Blueprint marked.** Every blueprint node of the track that carries
    70	`\lean{...}` also carries `\leanok`, or appears in the track's exemption table
    71	with a written reason; `scripts/blueprint_leanok_axioms.py --ci` exits 0. A
    72	node is any environment the repository's blueprint parser recognises: the gate
    73	reads that list out of `_TEX_ENV_BEGIN_RE` in `scripts/blueprint_lean_sync.py`
    74	instead of keeping its own, so an `example` or `remark` node with a Lean link
    75	counts exactly as a theorem does. Which nodes are the track's is read off the
    76	tree and not off section 6: besides the chapters registered there, the gate
    77	reads every other `.tex` beside them whose `\lean{...}` names a declaration
    78	under the track's Lean root, and judges those nodes too, so a node of the track
    79	that lives in a chapter shared with another track is in scope whether or not
    80	its chapter is listed. The
    81	exemption table is the only place a permanently unmarked node may live, and a
    82	row there is a caveat that must be defensible in the paper.
    83	
    84	**C5 — Lean comparator.** A comparator challenge exists covering every headline
    85	theorem; the in-repository expected challenge is free of regeneration drift
    86	(`scripts/comparator/check_challenge_drift.py` for that track's expected copy
    87	passes in CI); and the track's comparator record (§6, `docs/comparator.md`)
    88	states the challenge repository, the library commit that repository last
    89	verified with the official `leanprover/comparator` (`permitted_axioms` limited
    90	to the three standard axioms, external kernel check enabled where the platform
    91	allows), and the expected-copy path. That verified commit must be an
    92	ancestor-or-equal of the commit being declared finished, with no Lean change to
    93	the statement closure in between — which is exactly what a passing drift check
    94	proves.
    95	
    96	The coverage half of C5 is decided against the challenge, never against the
    97	record alone. The record's `expected-challenge` must be exactly the expected
    98	copy §6 registers for the track, and every headline theorem of §6 must occur in
    99	that file by its fully-qualified name — the name the assembler of
   100	`scripts/comparator/` writes for each declaration of the closure. A record that
   101	lists a headline theorem the registered expected copy never names fails C5:
   102	`covered-theorems` is written by hand in the same document, by the same session
   103	that wants to declare the track finished, so it may not be its own evidence.
   104	That the challenge *elaborates* to the same statements is the drift check and
   105	the comparator run, both delegated to CI.
   106	
   107	**C6 — Docs truthful.** No README, status page or estimate may advertise a
   108	nonzero open-site count once C1 holds. Every doc the track registers (§6) must
   109	exist: a registered doc that has been renamed or deleted fails C6 rather than
   110	being skipped, so the criterion can never report a green run over zero docs.
   111	
   112	**C7 — Artifact readiness.** "Done" means ready to be attached as an artifact
   113	to an ITP submission (owner, 2026-09-19), so every file such a submission needs
   114	is committed at the declared commit: the files §6 registers for the track —
   115	today `README.md`, `docs/QPBT-theorem-index.md`, `docs/DEVIATIONS.md`,
   116	`docs/ARTIFACT.md` and `LICENSE` — and the snapshot script
   117	`scripts/make_artifact.sh`. The gate checks that each of them exists and fails
   118	closed naming the missing ones; that the script *produces* a snapshot whose
   119	leak scan passes is a run, and is reported as delegated like C2, C4 and C5.
   120	A missing artifact file is main's to-do list, not a caveat that may be carried
   121	into a completion statement.
   122	
   123	## 3. Where the comparator challenge lives
   124	
   125	The challenge repository lives **outside** this repository and outside the
   126	umbrella repository: a separate repository of its own, as `LDT-comparator`
   127	already is for `MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.mainFormal` (`docs/comparator.md`). Three
   128	reasons, in order of weight:
   129	
   130	1. *Validating Proofs* level 4 requires the statement to be written in a
   131	   trusted environment separate from the proof code. A challenge inside this
   132	   repository would be elaborated in the same environment it is meant to check.
   133	2. The challenge must depend on this library **pinned by commit**. A repository
   134	   cannot meaningfully pin a commit of itself, and the pin is the evidence C5
   135	   rests on.
   136	3. `Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-qpbt` is the umbrella repository and is not the main
   137	   session's to modify (`local/personas/main.md`).
   138	
   139	What stays here: the generator (`scripts/comparator/`), the expected copy, the
   140	drift check, and the comparator record. Creating the challenge repository is an
   141	action outside this repository and is therefore an **owner action**, not a main
   142	decision.
   143	
   144	## 4. Who enforces this
   145	
   146	The main session, or the acting main, **may not** post a completion statement
   147	on the track's umbrella issues, close them, or tag a release unless
   148	
   149	    python3 scripts/completion_gate.py check --track <track>
   150	
   151	exits 0 on the exact commit being declared, and the gate's output is attached
   152	to the completion comment. A gate run on any other commit is not evidence.
   153	
   154	A failing gate is **not an owner blocker**. It is main's to-do list: no owner
   155	inbox comment is filed for it, and the work it names is ordinary development.
   156	
   157	The gate is deliberately **not** part of the blocking PR CI: it would fail every
   158	PR until the comparator challenge exists. `local/bin/ci.sh` has no non-blocking
   159	step class — every step it records is blocking — so CI is left unchanged, and
   160	the gate is run by hand before a completion statement.
   161	
   162	## 5. The gate
   163	
   164	`scripts/completion_gate.py` is python3, standard library only, no network and
   165	no model call. `check --track <t> [--repo-root R] [--commit C] [--json]` prints
   166	one PASS/FAIL line per criterion with `file:line` evidence, and exits 0 only
   167	when every mechanically checkable criterion passes. Criteria with a half that
   168	needs a run the gate does not perform (C2 axiom values, C4 `--ci` run, C5 drift
   169	regeneration, C7 snapshot leak scan) print as
   170	`DELEGATED` once their static half holds — never as `PASS`, so no completion
   171	comment can quote a green line for a check nobody ran — while a failing static
   172	half is still `FAIL`. `DELEGATED` does not turn a failing run green and does
   173	not by itself make one green either: the delegated halves are read off the CI
   174	run of the same commit. Unit tests:
   175	`scripts/tests/test_completion_gate.py`.
   176	
   177	## 6. Registered tracks
   178	
   179	### QPBT
   180	
   181	| Field | Value |
   182	|---|---|
   183	| Lean root | `MIPStarRE/QPBT` |
   184	| Blueprint chapters | `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch14_qpbt_observables.tex`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex` |
   185	| Paper-gap register | `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt-gap-register.md` |
   186	| Axiom audit | `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/AxiomAudit.lean` |
   187	| `\leanok` exemptions | `docs/completion/qpbt-leanok-exemptions.md` |
   188	| Comparator record | `docs/comparator.md`, block `track=qpbt` |
   189	| Expected challenge | `scripts/comparator/expected/ChallengeQPBT.lean.expected` |
   190	| Truthful docs (C6) | `README.md` |
   191	| Artifact files (C7) | `README.md`, `docs/QPBT-theorem-index.md`, `docs/DEVIATIONS.md`, `docs/ARTIFACT.md`, `LICENSE` |
   192	| Artifact script (C7) | `scripts/make_artifact.sh` |
   193	| Umbrella issues | 27, 168 |
   194	
   195	Headline theorems (blueprint chapter `ch13_qpbt_test.tex`):
   196	
   197	| Lean name | Blueprint node |
   198	|---|---|
   199	| `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness` | `thm:pauli` |
   200	| `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness_qubit` | `cor:pauli-binary` |
   201	| `MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_spcc_value_one` | `lem:pauli-completeness` |
   202	| `MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_ld_soundness` | `lem:ld-soundness` |
   203	
   204	The `Expected challenge` row and this table do not agree yet, and C5
   205	cannot go green until they do. The generator that writes that copy
   206	(`scripts/comparator/challenges.py`, the `targets` of its `qpbt` entry)
   207	covers two of the four headline theorems today — `pauli_soundness` and
   208	`pauli_soundness_qubit` — so the registered copy names neither
   209	`exists_spcc_value_one` nor `exists_ld_soundness`, and the coverage rule

   215	
   216	The `Blueprint chapters` row is the track's own chapters, read whole; it is

     3	Two challenges are configured, one per headline result: the LDT challenge

     5	`MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness` and `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness_qubit`.

     9	## The LDT challenge
    10	
    11	The headline theorem `MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.mainFormal` (the corrected source
    12	statement of `thm:main-formal` from the low individual degree test paper) is
    13	independently verifiable with the official
    14	[leanprover/comparator](https://github.com/leanprover/comparator), the
    15	top level of the escalating checks in the Lean reference manual's
    16	[Validating Proofs](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/ValidatingProofs/)
    17	chapter.
    18	
    19	Following community practice
    20	([lamplighter-comparator](https://github.com/vidick/lamplighter-comparator),
    21	[erdos-unit-distance-comparator](https://github.com/kim-em/erdos-unit-distance-comparator)),
    22	the challenge lives in a separate repository —
    23	**[LDT-comparator](https://github.com/LionSR/LDT-comparator)** —
    24	which requires this library as a lake dependency pinned by commit:
    25

    27	  and in dependency order, every declaration in the comparator-relevant
    28	  closure of the statement of `mainFormal` (111 declarations, ~1200 lines),

    30	  surface.

    32	  the same fully-qualified names; no bridging lemmas are needed.
    33	- Its CI runs the comparator (real landrun sandbox, nanoda external kernel,

    36	## What this repository contributes
    37	
    38	1. **Environment alignment.**  Comparator compares, constant by constant, the
    39	   full kernel closure of the statement — types, definition bodies, and the
    40	   proofs embedded in them — so `Challenge.lean` must elaborate to
    41	   bit-identical terms.  Every module contributing a declaration to the
    42	   closure therefore uses the full `import Mathlib` (directly or through
    43	   `MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/ParametersBase.lean` /
    44	   `MIPStarRE/Quantum/FiniteMatrix/Basic.lean`), so tactic elaboration sees
    45	   the same environment as the Mathlib-only `Challenge.lean`.  The four
    46	   modules with direct Mathlib imports carry a comment saying not to narrow
    47	   them.  (Measured impact: only 14 modules that did not already see full
    48	   Mathlib through `Quantum/FiniteMatrix/Basic.lean` gained it.)
    49	2. **Regeneration tooling.**  `scripts/comparator/` holds the closure
    50	   extractor (a Lean metaprogram mirroring comparator's `runForUsedConsts`)
    51	   and the assembler that produce `Challenge.lean`.  After changing any
    52	   definition in the closure: regenerate per `scripts/comparator/README.md`,
    53	   copy the result into LDT-comparator, and bump its library pin.
    54

    56	
    57	| Level | Requirement | Status |
    58	|---|---|---|
    59	| 2 | `#print axioms` shows only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound` | `MIPStarRE/LDT/Test/AxiomAudit.lean`; also enforced by comparator's `permitted_axioms` |
    60	| 3 | `lean4checker --fresh` re-check | `lean4checker: true` in the comparator repo's lean-action step |
    61	| 4 | Statement written in a trusted environment, separate from proof code | `Challenge.lean` imports only Mathlib (CI-enforced grep); separate repo, library pinned by commit |

    67	Deliberate deviations from the comparator README's adversarial setup, per its

    72	Residual trust: Lean's logical soundness, comparator's own plumbing, sandbox
    73	security, simultaneous bugs in all checkers, and human error in

    76	## The QPBT challenge
    77	
    78	The QPBT headline theorems `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness` (`thm:pauli`) and
    79	`MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness_qubit` (`cor:pauli-binary`) get the same
    80	treatment, in the separate repository
    81	**[QPBT-comparator](https://github.com/Dengnifer/QPBT-comparator)**.

    83	- **Targets.**  Both theorems are verified in one comparator run
    84	  (`theorem_names` lists both), so the challenge re-declares the union of the
    85	  two statement closures.

    87	  modules, about 2700 lines — larger than the LDT challenge because the

    95	### Environment alignment for QPBT
    96	
    97	Comparator compares the full kernel closure constant by constant, so the
    98	Mathlib-only challenge file must elaborate to bit-identical terms.  Two
    99	obstacles had to be removed in the library:
   100	
   101	1. **Narrowed imports.**  Four closure modules —
   102	   `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/Subspaces.lean`,
   103	   `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/Coefficients.lean`,
   104	   `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/LowDegreeCode.lean` and
   105	   `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/Lines.lean` — imported individual Mathlib files, so
   106	   tactic elaboration there saw a smaller environment than the challenge file
   107	   would.  They now use the full `import Mathlib` and carry the same "do not

   111	   `MIPStarRE/Quantum/FiniteMatrix/Basic.lean`.

   113	   qualified by its defining module (`_private.<module>.0.<name>`), so a

   115	   library's name.  Nineteen closure members were private — twelve in

   120	   `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/Pauli.lean`.  Dropping `private` is the smallest

   122	   the visibility of names that the statement closure already depends on.

   129	`MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/Distribution.lean`,

   137	
   138	Regeneration is the pipeline in `scripts/comparator/README.md` with

   144	What the human must audit, and what no tool can check: that
   145	`ChallengeQPBT.lean` really states the intended theorems.  Concretely, that

   153	
   154	## Benchmark use
   155	
   156	The same statement is submission-ready for
   157	[leanprover/lean-eval](https://github.com/leanprover/lean-eval) (the official
   158	comparator-based benchmark behind [lean-lang.org/eval](https://lean-lang.org/eval/)):
   159	port the statement module to lean-eval's toolchain, tag the theorem
   160	`@[eval_problem]`, add a `manifests/problems/<id>.toml` (`holes`, `submitter`,
   161	`source`, `informal_solution`), and open a PR to lean-eval.  Large
   162	self-contained statement preludes have precedent there (the knot-theory
   163	problems ship a 23 KB trusted `ChallengeDeps.lean`).  Solvers edit only
   164	`Submission.lean`; scoring is comparator acceptance, with submissions run by

     7	
     8	`MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness` is an implication: for every admissible
     9	parameter tuple `P`, every `ε ≥ 0` and every strategy `S` for
    10	`pauliBasisTest P` with `1 - ε ≤ S.value`, extraction data exist whose three
    11	error quantities are bounded by `deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q`.  A reader is
    12	entitled to ask two questions about such a statement, and this module answers
    13	both with citable declarations.  Nothing here changes or restates an existing
    14	definition or theorem; every result is a corollary of material already on the
    15	main development.

    17	## Q1 — are the hypotheses satisfiable?
    18	
    19	`AdmissibleParams` is inhabited (`nonVacuousParams`, and hence
    20	`nonempty_admissibleParams`), and for *every* admissible `P` the honest
    21	strategy of `lem:pauli-completeness` is a strategy for `pauliBasisTest P`
    22	itself with value exactly `1` (`exists_pauliBasisTest_strategy_value_one`);
    23	the symmetric presentation used by `exists_spcc_value_one` has
    24	`pauliBasisTest P` as its underlying game definitionally
    25	(`pauliBasisTestSymm_toGame`).  Consequently the hypothesis triple
    26	`0 ≤ ε`, `S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P)`, `1 - ε ≤ S.value` is jointly
    27	satisfiable — with `ε = 0`, the strongest case
    28	(`pauli_soundness_hypotheses_satisfiable`) — and `pauli_soundness` applied to
    29	it yields an unconditional statement
    30	(`pauli_soundness_applies_to_honest_strategy`).
    31	
    32	## Q2 — is the conclusion non-trivial?
    33	
    34	The bound is `deltaQld a b ε m d q = a * (m*d)^a * (ε^b + q^(-b) + 2^(-b*m*d))`
    35	with `a, b` existentially quantified by the theorem, so no *single* numeric
    36	value can be extracted.  What can be shown, and is shown here, is that

    35	noncomputable def deltaQld (a b ε : ℝ) (m d q : ℕ) : ℝ :=
    36	  a * Real.rpow ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) a *
    37	    (Real.rpow ε b + Real.rpow (q : ℝ) (-b) +
    38	      Real.rpow 2 (-(b * ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ))))

    43	`rem:pauli-robustness-form` and stated as `lem:delta-qld-mono-support`,
    44	blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex`; the source makes this constant adjustment

    46	not an additional hypothesis of `thm:pauli` or `lem:qld-4-7`. -/

    48	    (ha0 : 1 ≤ a) (ha : a ≤ a') (hb : b' ≤ b) (hb' : 0 < b')
    49	    (hε0 : 0 ≤ ε) (hε1 : ε ≤ 1) :
    50	    deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q ≤ deltaQld a' b' ε P.m P.d P.q := by
    51	  have hmd : (1 : ℝ) ≤ ((P.m * P.d : ℕ) : ℝ) :=
    52	    Nat.one_le_cast.mpr (Nat.mul_pos P.one_le_m P.hd)
    53	  have hmd0 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ ((P.m * P.d : ℕ) : ℝ) := by linarith
    54	  have hq : (1 : ℝ) ≤ (P.q : ℝ) := by
    55	    obtain ⟨k, -, hk⟩ := P.hq
    56	    rw [hk]
    57	    exact_mod_cast Nat.one_le_pow _ _ (by norm_num)
    58	  unfold deltaQld
    59	  simp only [Real.rpow_eq_pow]
    60	  have h1 : ((P.m * P.d : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ a ≤ ((P.m * P.d : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ a' :=

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# estimate.sh — 8-hourly completion estimate for track A (owner request 2026-09-04).
# Posts ONE two-line comment on the pinned "Completion estimate" issue and appends a JSON line
# to results/telemetry/estimates.jsonl. Method (count-based): 197 stage-4.3 obligations at the
# start (171 on main at takeover + 26 in the chapter-16 skeleton); implemented% = closed/197;
# days-to-go = open sites / sites closed on main in the trailing 24 h (lower bound: the
# remaining sites are the harder ones). Sites proved in open PRs are deduplicated across
# stacked PRs.
set -u
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

# `grep -c sorry` also matches prose: MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/StrategyClasses.lean
# and MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Apply.lean each explain their hole in a
# docstring, so the open-obligation number posted on the tracker issue used to
# be larger than the number of real sites.

# rule of scripts/audit_stale_issues.py (`line_is_sorry` with `_SORRY_LINE_RE`),
# which drops `--` line comments before matching.  This script scans whole files
# instead of issue-cited lines, so it additionally anchors the token to the
# tactic/term positions it can occupy: a bare `sorry` line (optionally after a
# `·` bullet), `:= sorry`, `by sorry`, and `(sorry)`.  Keep the two in sync.

     3	This page is for two audiences: a **reviewer** who received the artifact
     4	tarball and wants to check that the claimed theorems really are proved, and a
     5	**maintainer** who has to cut the next snapshot.

     7	The artifact is a **release snapshot of the mathematical development**, not the

    91	## Verifying the artifact as a reviewer
    92	
    93	### 1. Install the pinned toolchain
    94	
    95	```sh
    96	curl https://elan.lean-lang.org/elan-init.sh -sSf | sh   # if elan is not installed
    97	cd <unpacked snapshot>
    98	cat lean-toolchain     # leanprover/lean4:v4.32.0 — elan installs this on first use
    99	```
   100	
   101	### 2. Fetch the Mathlib build cache and build
   102	
   103	```sh
   104	lake exe cache get
   105	lake build MIPStarRE.QPBT
   106	```
   107	
   108	**Expected cost.** `lake exe cache get` downloads several GB. Plan on **16 GB
   109	of RAM** and tens of GB of disk. At this source commit, these commands count
   110	occurrences and files, respectively:
   111	
   112	```sh
   113	rg -n -o 'maxHeartbeats' MIPStarRE | wc -l
   114	rg -l 'maxHeartbeats' MIPStarRE | wc -l
   115	rg -n -o 'synthInstance\.maxSize' MIPStarRE | wc -l
   116	rg -l 'synthInstance\.maxSize' MIPStarRE | wc -l
   117	```
   118	
   119	They report 38 occurrences across 23 files for `maxHeartbeats`, and 66 across
   120	17 files for `synthInstance.maxSize`, so this is not a laptop build. Honest
   121	statement of the evidence we have: the maintainers' build telemetry records
   122	1,608 builds of this development, but every one is an
   123	*incremental, warm-cache* build (the two most recent took 79 s and 556 s); the
   124	only full-rebuild record, 25,052 s (7 h), is from 2026-08-30 and predates most
   125	of the QPBT development. **A cold clean-clone build of `MIPStarRE.QPBT` has not
   126	yet been recorded**; when one is, its wall-clock time and machine replace this
   127	paragraph. Budget several hours.
   128	
   129	### 3. Check that nothing is assumed
   130	
   131	The development claims to depend on no axioms beyond Lean's three standard
   132	ones — `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound` — and on no `sorry`,
   133	`admit`, `native_decide`, `unsafe` or `@[extern]` escape hatch.
   134	
   135	The check that settles the first half is Lean's own `#print axioms`: it reports
   136	the complete axiom closure of a declaration, and unlike a text search it cannot
   137	be misled by prose. The snapshot ships two modules that run it at build time and
   138	**fail the build** when a declaration's closure is not exactly
   139	`{Classical.choice, Quot.sound, propext}` — one for the Pauli test, one for the
   140	classical low-individual-degree layer underneath it:
   141	
   142	```sh
   143	lake build MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.AxiomAudit
   144	lake build MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.AxiomAudit
   145	```
   146	
   147	`MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.AxiomAudit` covers the four headline theorems of section 4
   148	and nine further load-bearing statements; the printed axiom lines stay in the
   149	build log as the positive record. Neither module is imported from the
   150	`MIPStarRE.QPBT` umbrella — that keeps the audits out of ordinary downstream
   151	imports — so a plain `lake build MIPStarRE.QPBT` does not run them and they have
   152	to be named, as above.
   153	
   154	To read the closures directly instead, put this in a scratch file at the root of
   155	the unpacked snapshot and elaborate it with `lake env lean scratch.lean`:
   156	
   157	```lean
   158	import MIPStarRE.QPBT
   159	
   160	#print axioms MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness
   161	#print axioms MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness_qubit
   162	#print axioms MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_spcc_value_one
   163	#print axioms MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_ld_soundness
   164	```
   165	
   166	Each of the four must report exactly `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.
   167	A `sorryAx` in a closure would mean the theorem is not proved; a project
   168	`axiom` would appear in the list under its own name.
   169	
   170	`#print axioms` does not report `native_decide`, `unsafe` or `@[extern]`, which
   171	move trust outside the kernel without leaving an axiom behind. A text search is
   172	the check for those, and for `axiom` declarations:
   173	
   174	```sh
   175	grep -rn --include='*.lean' -E '^[[:space:]]*axiom |\b(sorry|admit|native_decide|unsafe)\b|@\[extern' MIPStarRE/
   176	```
   177	
   178	**Expected output: a handful of matches, every one of them inside a comment or
   179	a docstring that discusses an escape hatch rather than using one.** At the
   180	commit named in `MANIFEST.txt` there are four: three are the word `sorry` in
   181	backticks — `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Apply.lean`, describing a source proof
   182	that was open in the paper, and the two audit modules named above, whose prose
   183	says what they exist to catch — and one is a docstring line in
   184	`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/QubitForm.lean` that happens to begin with the word
   185	"axiom". A match in code position — a bare `sorry` in
   186	tactic position, or a line that really begins a declaration with `axiom` —
   187	would be a genuine escape hatch. `grep` cannot tell prose from code, which is
   188	why the `#print axioms` run above is the check that counts.
   189

   273	## Keeping the two exclusion lists in step
   274	
   275	What ships is decided twice, on purpose:
   276	
   277	- `INCLUDE` / `EXCLUDE` in `scripts/make_artifact.sh` — an explicit allow-list,
   278	  so a new top-level directory never joins the artifact by accident;
   279	- the `export-ignore` attributes in `.gitattributes` — applied by `git archive`
   280	  itself, so a plain `git archive` or a GitHub source tarball is clean too.
   281	
   282	A path excluded in one should be excluded in the other, and the second guard is
   283	the weaker of the two: it is a deny-list, so a new workflow-only file has to be
   284	added to it by hand, whereas the allow-list drops anything it has not been told
   285	about. `scripts/` is the one mixed directory — three entries ship, the roughly
   286	thirty workflow-only ones do not — and `git archive` does not descend into a
   287	directory it has been told to ignore, so a child of an ignored directory cannot
   288	be re-admitted. The deny-list therefore excludes the workflow-only scripts by
   289	glob (`scripts/*.py`, `scripts/*.sh`, `scripts/*.lean`, `scripts/tests/`) and
   290	re-admits the two shipped top-level files with `-export-ignore`;
   291	`scripts/comparator/` is never matched and ships under both guards.
   292	`references/` is named in `.gitattributes` too, as a comment rather than an
   293	`export-ignore` line, so that the decision to ship it is visible where somebody
   294	would otherwise add the line back. Checked again on 2026-09-21 at the final PR

When the direction is nonzero and $x_{\overline w}$ lies on the line, exactly one such $t$ exists and the formulation above agrees with the source. But zero directions occur: Definition~\ref{def:line} explicitly permits them, and the question distribution of Definition~\ref{def:ld-question-distribution} produces $\mathsf{DLine}$ questions with $v' = \pi_{i-1}(v) = 0$ with positive probability, namely whenever the last $m - i + 1$ coordinates of $v$ vanish. In that case $\ell(u_0, 0) = \{u_0\}$, every $t \in \F_q$ satisfies $x_{\overline w} = u_0 + t v'$ when $x_{\overline w} = u_0$, and the source clause does not determine acceptance for a nonconstant answer polynomial. Completeness is unaffected: the restriction of a polynomial $g$ to the singleton line $\ell(u_0,0)$, expressed through the parameterization $t \mapsto u_0 + t \cdot 0$, is the constant polynomial with value $g(u_0)$, which passes the check for every $t$. docs/blueprint_style_guide.md:179:**Statement-level `\leanok`.** Place this inside a `theorem`, `lemma`, `proposition`, `corollary`, or `definition` environment, on its own line immediately after `\lean{...}`. It says that the corresponding Lean declaration exists and that its statement matches the blueprint or paper statement. It does **not** say that the Lean proof already exists or is complete. For definitions, this is the only `\leanok` marker.
docs/blueprint_style_guide.md:181:**Proof-level `\leanok`.** Place this inside the matching `proof` environment, preferably as the first line after `\begin{proof}`. The canonical current placement is the theorem `thm:commutativity-points` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch08_commutativity.tex:8-19`, where the statement block has `\leanok` immediately after `\lean{...}` and the proof block begins with another `\leanok`. This marker says that the Lean proof is complete and free of unresolved `sorry` or unjustified project-level `axiom` shortcuts. In particular, `#print axioms <decl>` must show no `sorryAx`, and the declaration must satisfy the broader blocker rules in the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and [`docs/project_conventions.md`](project_conventions.md).
docs/blueprint_style_guide.md:183:A theorem, lemma, proposition, or corollary node is **fully formalized in Lean if and only if it has both markers**: statement-level `\leanok` in the statement block and proof-level `\leanok` in the proof block. Statement-level without proof-level means “the statement has been transcribed and matched, but the proof is not yet certified complete.” Definitions have no proof block, so statement-level `\leanok` alone is enough there.
docs/blueprint_style_guide.md:200:**Current CI behavior.** The advisory Blueprint ↔ Lean sync check in [`docs/ci-blueprint-sync.md`](https://github.com/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A/blob/main/docs/ci-blueprint-sync.md) distinguishes the two placements. Only proof-level `\leanok` whose axiom closure contains `sorryAx` (or whose harness output cannot be parsed) is reported as an **error**. Statement-level-only `\leanok` with the same finding is downgraded to a **warning**, because statement-level does not claim proof completeness. Each audit line is annotated with the observed placement so reviewers can tell statement-sync work apart from proof-completion work.

   573	
   574	There remains a theorem-level gap in the source proof route.  The classical
   575	low individual degree game invoked at dimension $2m+2$ is undefined for every
   576	admissible tuple with $m \ge 2$ (and for $(q,m)=(2,1)$), because its question
   577	distribution requires $2m+2 \mid q$ while admissibility supplies only
   578	$m \mid q$.  Independently, the source import still requires a reduction to
   579	the two-prover tensor-code test with a value bound and a valid choice of
   580	$K \ge 12m'(d+1)$; the printed choice $K=(m')^3d$ fails at the small
   581	dimensions listed in Section~\ref{sec:import-obligations}.

   583	Soundness of the directly indexed game is now established at arbitrary
   584	dimension by a different proof through the low individual degree theorem and
   585	the general-simultaneity combining reduction.  That proof checks the separate
   586	condition $400Md \le N$ for $M=m'+\kappa$ and $N=2560000M^3d$.  It neither
   587	applies the tensor-code theorem nor verifies its bound on $K$, so it bypasses
   588	rather than discharges both source-import obligations.  The correlated-residue

   591	Schwartz--Zippel recover the global relation on the original Hilbert spaces,

   593	double-compression identity.

   595	still has its declared construction and carrier-transport obligations; repairing
   596	the original tensor-code import would provide another route to soundness.  We
   597	do not assert that either conclusion is false; the open points are verification

    10	\title{Documenting Possible Gaps, Counterexamples, and Formalization Deviations}
    11	\author{}
    12	\date{2026-04-29}
    13	
    14	\begin{document}
    15	\maketitle
    16	
    17	\section{Purpose}
    18	
    19	When a formalization relies on a cited mathematical source, the cited source
    20	should remain intact.  It is a source, not an errata file.  If a possible gap,
    21	missing hypothesis, incorrect numerical constant, or other mathematical
    22	discrepancy is found, the matter should be recorded in a separate LaTeX note.
    23	In this repository such notes live under \path{docs/paper-gaps/}.  The same
    24	principle applies when the formal development has already diverged from the
    25	cited source, for instance by changing a statement so that it compiles, or by
    26	using a different mathematical route because an available formal-library theorem
    27	has a slightly different form.  Such a note is a mathematical note first, and a
    28	record of the formalization second: it should be readable by a mathematician or
    29	mathematical physicist who has not followed the issue discussion.
    30	
    31	The note should isolate the mathematical mechanism.  It should say what the
    32	cited source asserts, what the cited results actually imply, where a term or
    33	hypothesis is lost, and what statement the formal development proves instead.
    34	If the formal proof takes a different route, the note should explain the
    35	replacement argument and the hypotheses on which it rests.  This is especially
    36	important when the proof uses a theorem, construction, or convention from
    37	Mathlib which is not part of the cited argument.  In that case the note should
    38	state the Mathlib result in ordinary mathematical language, explain how it is
    39	specialized to the notation of the paper, and compare its hypotheses and
    40	conclusion with the step it replaces.  It should not merely say that \Lean{} did
    41	not accept a proof, that the modified proof compiles, or that a named library
    42	lemma was applied.
    43	
    44	The documents in this directory should themselves follow this standard.  A
    45	policy or template which reads like a checklist will tend to produce checklist
    46	notes; the examples and templates should therefore be written as mathematical
    47	prose.
    48	
    49	\section{Concision and Readability}
    50	
    51	A paper-gap note should be short enough that a reader can understand the issue
    52	in one sitting.  The first page should answer four questions: what the source
    53	uses, how hard the remaining formal work is, what the formalization or audit
    54	checked, and what the current verdict is.  Begin with a short
    55	\emph{At a glance} section when the note concerns an open or recently resolved
    56	formalization task.  That section should estimate the difficulty, the rough
    57	implementation weight, the split between Mathlib reuse and project-local work,
    58	and the key Mathlib APIs or modules.  Use honest ranges, not false precision.
    59	
    60	The \emph{Key theorem forms} section should be Section~2, immediately after
    61	\emph{At a glance}.  Put the theorem forms before the source details so the
    62	reader knows what the formalization is aiming to prove.  After that, keep the
    63	source assertion, the mechanism being checked, the blueprint/formal comparison,
    64	and the conclusion.  Use more sections only when a counterexample or long
    65	derivation genuinely needs room.
    66	
    67	Keep background to the minimum needed for the local point.  Prefer one clear
    68	special case over a general restatement of the surrounding theorem.  Use displayed
    69	equations for the source assertion, the key calculation, and the theorem forms;
    70	avoid displays for traceability data, declaration names, or long lists.  The
    71	blueprint/formal comparison should be compact and should not repeat the theorem
    72	forms.  The section ``Form of the Note'' below specifies where traceability data
    73	belongs; the body should read as mathematical prose, not as a log.
    74	
    75	If the verdict is that there is no mathematical discrepancy, say so plainly and
    76	stop.  Keep the conclusion highly compact, normally under twenty source lines.
    77	If the only remaining work is an implementation task, name it briefly and link
    78	the issue or pull request in a footnote.
    79	
    80	\section{When the Investigation Starts}
    81	
    82	The investigation starts when the obstruction appears to be mathematical rather
    83	than merely formal.  No final judgement is needed at this stage.  It is enough
    84	that, after reading the relevant source and attempting the corresponding formal
    85	statement, the proof seems to require a different scalar, an additional
    86	hypothesis, a different tensor placement, a distinction between two objects which
    87	the prose identifies, or an auxiliary assertion not supplied by the cited
    88	argument.
    89	
    90	The same investigation should also start when such a deviation is discovered
    91	after the fact.  If the existing formal development or informal blueprint has
    92	already changed the statement, strengthened a hypothesis, weakened a conclusion,
    93	inserted an unadvertised lemma, or replaced the cited proof by a different
    94	formal-library argument, the mathematical change should be documented even if all
    95	relevant files already compile.
    96	
    97	At this early stage the purpose is to preserve the question while it is still
    98	local.  The note may later conclude that the matter is only notational, that an
    99	intermediate estimate in the cited source needs a harmless correction, that a
   100	missing hypothesis is genuinely needed, or that no discrepancy remains.  Thus
   101	the trigger is not the severity of the eventual verdict, but the appearance of a
   102	real mismatch between the cited reasoning and the statement that can be
   103	formalized.
   104	
   105	A failed tactic search, a missing formal lemma, or an inconvenient coercion is
   106	not enough.  The obstruction must survive translation back into ordinary
   107	mathematics.
   108	
   109	Once a cited statement is established to be mathematically false, the repair
   110	and decision procedure is governed by Section~6 of
   111	\path{local/protocols/issues-prs.md}.  A dedicated mathematical-gap session must
   112	produce a correction which is correct, sufficient for every paper and blueprint
   113	use, and minimal, then iterate it against the Lean statement and its downstream
   114	consumers.  Astra availability has been reported, so the current Codex route is
   115	\texttt{dispatch.sh --role mathfix} with Astra; historical owner-launched
   116	Fable~5.1 measurements remain unchanged.  Main decides and records mathematical
   117	nonconvergence and any required correction to a definition or game, with the
   118	source semantics preserved and subject to the faithfulness audit and
   119	independent mathematical review that Section~6 requires.  These project
   120	outcomes do not become owner blockers merely because the formalization might
   121	otherwise fail.
   122	
   123	Pinned owner inbox~\#500 is used only when an action needs owner permission
   124	because its risk extends beyond project development, such as changing owner
   125	files, the machine or its accounts, spending money, or acting outside this
   126	repository.  Each blocker is one comment with at most ten visible lines in
   127	plain language: one line saying what is stuck, lettered one-line options, one
   128	recommendation, and the literal reply
   129	\texttt{DECISION B<n>: <letter>}.  Ids continue after B11, additional detail is
   130	folded, and the immutable \texttt{owner-inbox id=B<n>} marker keys creation and
   131	resolution of the same comment.  Resolution changes the separate body field to
   132	\texttt{owner-inbox-status=closed} and adds \texttt{RESOLVED B<n>}.  Issue~\#26
   133	is archived and receives no new comments.
   134	
   135	Sometimes an investigation uncovers an improvement that is not a discrepancy:
   136	the formalization works correctly, but it could be simplified by using an
   137	existing library, replacing a custom type, or adopting a cleaner proof route.
   138	These are not, by themselves, paper-gap notes.  They are action items.  When
   139	such an improvement is identified, open a GitHub issue or pull request that
   140	describes the proposed change.  If the investigation also produces a paper-gap
   141	note, link the issue or pull request from that note: the note records the
   142	mathematical justification, and the issue or pull request drives the
   143	implementation.
   144	
   145	\section{When to Write a Note}
   146	
   147	A note should be written once the source argument and the formal proof no longer
   148	match as mathematical arguments.  This includes, for instance, a numerical
   149	estimate whose constant does not follow from the cited lemma, a displayed
   150	conclusion which uses an unstated hypothesis, or a step in which two objects are
   151	identified although they must remain distinct.  In analytic, algebraic,
   152	probabilistic, or quantum arguments, such distinctions may concern the domain of
   153	a map, the placement of a tensor factor, the type of an outcome, the distinction
   154	between a structure and a substructure, or the scalar carried by an approximation
   155	relation.
   156	
   157	A note is required when an audit finds that a Lean declaration associated with a
   158	source-labelled statement has acquired an extra non-source hypothesis, such as
   159	bridge, residual, repair, producer, or obligation-structure data.  Such a
   160	declaration is temporary proof debt, not a replacement for the source theorem,
   161	and should not be introduced merely to avoid a \verb|sorry|.  The note must say
   162	plainly that the Lean result is conditional, identify the source-faithful theorem
   163	form that remains to be proved, and give the intended obligation discharger or
   164	removal plan.  The blueprint should not mark the source-labelled statement with
   165	\verb|\leanok| by pointing to this conditional helper.
   166	
   167	Changing a Lean theorem away from the statement in
   168	\path{references/ldt-paper/} is strongly discouraged.  A paper-gap note should
   169	not make such a change look routine: it should explain the mathematical
   170	necessity, or else classify the change as proof debt to be removed.
   171	
   172	When an existing conditional helper is audited, the first task is to extract any
   173	argument it already contains into source-faithful lemmas.  If the remaining
   174	bridge hypothesis cannot be derived from the paper hypotheses, the formal
   175	development should restore the source theorem statement and record the missing
   176	proof obligation explicitly, rather than retaining the strengthened statement as
   177	though it were the paper theorem.
   178	
   179	This requirement is not meant to classify every explicit Lean side condition as
   180	a discrepancy.  Positivity, nonemptiness, decidability, field-model instances,
   181	and denominator nonvanishing hypotheses may be faithful encodings of the domain
   182	in which the paper's theorem is stated.  The note should distinguish such
   183	boundary hypotheses from hypotheses that supply an unproved step of the paper
   184	argument.
   185	
   186	A note is also appropriate when the proof becomes formal only after changing an
   187	intermediate scalar, weakening a conclusion, strengthening a hypothesis, or
   188	inserting an additional lemma which is not simply an expansion of the cited
   189	argument.  These are mathematical changes, even when they are harmless for the
   190	final theorem.  It is likewise appropriate when an available formal-library
   191	theorem proves the needed result under a somewhat different formulation from the
   192	cited source.  In that case the note should be deliberately pedagogical.  It
   193	should explain, in ordinary mathematical language, what the replacement result
   194	says, how it is specialized, which hypotheses are new or differently packaged,
   195	and why the resulting statement is a legitimate substitute for the step in the
   196	cited argument.  If the issue remains open after reasonable attempts, the note
   197	should say what has been checked and what remains unknown.
   198	
   199	\section{Counterexamples}
   200	
   201	If the cited assertion appears to be false, the note should not stop at saying
   202	that the proof cannot be formalized.  It should give the counterexample, or the
   203	smallest relevant part of it, in ordinary mathematical notation.  The example
   204	should be accompanied by enough verification that the reader can see both sides:
   205	the hypotheses of the cited assertion hold, and its conclusion fails.
   206	
   207	When feasible, the counterexample should also be formalized in \Lean{}.  This is
   208	especially valuable when the example is finite, algebraic, computational, or
   209	otherwise small enough that the failure can be checked without reproducing the
   210	whole surrounding theory.  The note should then state the mathematical content
   211	of the checked counterexample and identify the corresponding Lean declaration in
   212	a footnote.  The Lean file is not a substitute for the prose: the prose should
   213	still explain why the example refutes the cited assertion.
   214	
   215	\section{Revision of a Note}
   216	
   217	A paper-gap note may be provisional.  It may begin as soon as the mathematical
   218	obstruction has been isolated well enough to state the question, and it may be
   219	revised as the calculation, the blueprint, or the corresponding \Lean{}
   220	declarations become clearer.  The first version need not know the final
   221	classification, but it should say plainly which mathematical point is known and
   222	which point remains unsettled.
   223	
   224	Later revisions should not make the note into a chronological log.  They should
   225	rewrite the document so that it remains a coherent account of the present
   226	mathematical understanding.  If the verdict changes, the conclusion should state
   227	the current verdict; the linked issue or pull request can preserve the earlier
   228	discussion.
   229	
   230	\section{Form of the Note}
   231	
   232	Each note should stand on its own.  It should give the date, cite the relevant
   233	source article, and provide enough traceability for the reader to locate the
   234	original passage and the project discussion.  GitHub issues and pull requests may
   235	be linked with \verb|\href|, and source files, line ranges, and labels should be
   236	recorded when they help the reader check the claim.  These references should
   237	serve the exposition rather than govern it: the main text should be organized
   238	around the mathematical assertion and its proof.
   239	
   240	The note should introduce its notation before using it.  Symbols for
   241	measurements, tensor factors, approximation relations, and error parameters
   242	should be named in prose.  If an approximation relation is state-dependent, the
   243	state should be named, or its defining expression should be given when this can
   244	be done briefly.  Only after the notation is in place should the note state the
   245	assertion in the cited source, using a bibliographic citation such as
   246	\verb|\cite[Section~...]{...}| when the section or chapter is known.
   247	
   248	Only the relevant hypotheses should be reproduced.  If the question is a scalar
   249	substitution, a missing term, or a missing hypothesis, the note should not quote
   250	a long unrelated part of the proof.  It should give the cited lemma or
   251	proposition in the special case actually used, then display the calculation or
   252	logical implication in which the discrepancy appears.
   253	
   254	Displayed equations should be used with restraint.  They are appropriate for the
   255	source estimate being checked, the cited estimate in the form actually used, and
   256	the calculation where a term or hypothesis appears or disappears.  When a
   257	displayed equation is identified by a source label, the label should appear on
   258	the right of the display, while the surrounding prose refers to the mathematical
   259	assertion itself.  The standard \texttt{amsmath} command \verb|\tag| is the
   260	right mechanism for this; a separate local convention should be introduced only
   261	if the standard mechanism is genuinely insufficient.  For a multi-line aligned
   262	display, tag the individual lines that carry the source information rather than
   263	forcing a long combined label below the equations.  Short
   264	scalar definitions and elementary inequalities should remain inline when the
   265	sentence reads better that way.  As in ordinary mathematical writing, a displayed
   266	formula is part of the surrounding sentence and should be punctuated accordingly.
   267	
   268	Bibliographic entries used only by these notes should live in
   269	\path{docs/paper-gaps/references.bib}.  A new note should ordinarily begin from
   270	\path{docs/paper-gaps/template.tex}, which records the common LaTeX preamble,
   271	the local bibliography, and a model for right-hand source labels in displayed
   272	equations.
   273	
   274	Blueprint prose cites a note like any other source, with
   275	\verb|\cite{gap:<slug>}|; the bibliography entry in
   276	\path{blueprint/src/references.bib} carries the published URL of the note,
   277	whether the note lives in this repository or in another one.  Lean docstrings
   278	and comments use the repository path form \path{docs/paper-gaps/<slug>.tex}.
   279	
   280	The note should then compare the cited source with the informal blueprint, if
   281	there is one, and with the formal statement.  This comparison should be written
   282	in ordinary mathematical prose.  Formal declaration names and source paths should
   283	be supplied only to identify the exact formal statements, and normally belong in
   284	footnotes.
   285	
   286	The conclusion should give a verdict.  It may say that there is no discrepancy,
   287	that the matter is only notational, that an intermediate estimate needs a
   288	harmless correction, that a hypothesis is missing, that there is a theorem-level
   289	gap, or that the question remains open.  The classification should reflect the
   290	mathematics, not the amount of formal work required.
   291	
   292	\section{Decision Principle}
   293	
   294	The formal development should not silently replace the cited assertion by a
   295	different one.  If the formal statement differs from the cited source, the
   296	reason for the difference should be written down.  Conversely, the note should
   297	not overstate the conclusion.  A wrong intermediate scalar is not a fatal gap in
   298	the theorem if the corrected scalar is bounded by the error parameter appearing
   299	in the theorem statement.
